title: Maximum Product Difference Between Two Pairs
summary: The product difference between pairs (a, b) and (c, d) is calculated as (a * b) - (c * d).
statement: The product difference between pairs (a, b) and (c, d) is calculated as (a * b) - (c * d). Given an array, select four unique indices to maximize the product difference between the pairs (nums[w], nums[x]) and (nums[y], nums[z]). Return the highest product difference.
constraints: 4 <= len(nums) <= 10000 and all values are positive.
Choose four distinct indices for two products.
hints: Positive products grow with either factor.
Sort the values; maximize the added product with the two largest and minimize the subtracted product with the two smallest.
The four selected indices are distinct because the array has at least four elements, and monotonicity of positive multiplication proves both extreme choices.
editorial: The four selected indices are distinct because the array has at least four elements, and monotonicity of positive multiplication proves both extreme choices.

tests.explanation: The two largest values produce 42 and the two smallest produce 8, giving 34.
Products 9*8 and 2*4 give the maximum difference 64.
